# Day 7 -- Machine Learning Models, and the Full Model Comparison

**Generated by** `src/evaluation/run_ml.py`. 
Every number is produced by running the pipeline -- none is asserted.

All **seven** candidates (3 baselines + 2 statistical + 2 ML) were run in a 
single `run_walk_forward` call per target, on the identical 65 folds, so 
common support spans the whole comparison. This is the roadmap's Day-7 
validation checkpoint: the complete model-comparison matrix.

---

## 1. How the ML models are built

**Direct multi-horizon** (addendum Section 2): a separate estimator per 
horizon learns `X[t] -> y[t+lead]` directly, so a 14-period forecast never 
compounds 14 one-step errors. This is deliberately unlike SARIMAX/ETS, which 
fit once and read all three horizons off one recursive path.

Training pairs for a fold with window `[start .. cutoff]`:

```
{ (X[t], y[t + lead]) : start <= t  AND  t + lead <= cutoff }
```

The `t + lead <= cutoff` half is load-bearing -- without it a training pair 
would carry a label from after the training cutoff, i.e. the model would be 
trained on the future it is about to predict. It costs `lead` rows off the end 
of every window, so h=14 always trains on fewer pairs than h=1.

| Setting | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Predictors | 57 engineered columns (lags, rolling stats, calendar) | roadmap Part 3: upstream series usable "only in lagged/rolling form" |
| Random Forest | 300 trees, depth 8, min_samples_leaf 5, max_features sqrt | config; light and time-boxed, no search |
| Gradient Boosting | `HistGradientBoostingRegressor`, 300 iters, depth 4, lr 0.05 | addendum Section 4 (NOT the classic class) |
| Seed | 42 on every stochastic fit | addendum Section 3 |
| Early stopping | disabled | an internal validation split would be a RANDOM split of a time series |
| Min training pairs | 30 | abstain rather than fit on too little |

## 2. Missing-data handling, and one finding

The addendum specifies asymmetric treatment: Random Forest **drops** feature 
rows containing NaN (count logged); HistGradientBoosting **keeps** them and 
handles NaN natively.

**Finding:** scikit-learn added native missing-value support for tree ensembles 
in 1.4, so on the installed version `RandomForestRegressor` no longer *requires* 
the drop -- the addendum was written when it did. The drop is retained as the 
governing methodological rule rather than silently abandoned, which also keeps 
the intended contrast between the two families. `requirements.txt` now pins 
`scikit-learn>=1.4.0`, since the prediction path relies on that behaviour.

Training rows dropped by the Random Forest NaN rule are counted per fold and 
carried in `forecasts/ml_predictions.csv`. Folds where the RF prediction row 
itself contained a NaN: **10 of 65** -- always from a flow-derived lag. RF still 
forecasts there (see `RANDOM_FOREST_ABSTAINS_ON_NAN_PREDICTION_ROW` in config 
for why abstaining would have been an invented extra handicap that shrank the 
whole seven-way comparison by 15%).
